newsitem.title: USA: Kmart signs pact for appliances, housewares.
newsitem.headline: Kmart signs pact for appliances, housewares.

text.p: Kmart Corp said on Monday it signed an agreement with Salton/Maxim Housewares Inc and New M-Tech Corp to supply Kmart with a broad range of small electrical appliances and consumer electronics under the White-Westinghouse brand name.

Kmart said the agreement, effective immediately, makes it the exclusive U.S. mass merchant retailer of a broad range of White-Westinghouse brand kitchen housewares, personal care products, electronics and other products.
Both Salton/Maxim and New M-Tech are 50 percent-owned by Windmere-Durable Holdings Inc.

Cindy Solovei, assistant vice president of finance for Windmere, said the contract confirmed terms disclosed by the company in December, calling for $1.7 billion in purchases by Kmart over seven years.

Under certain circumstances, the minimum can drop to $1.4 billion, but the contract also may be extended for an additional nine years and $2.5 billion worth of purchases, making the deal worth a potential $4.2 billion.
Solovei said the contract will prevent Salton/Maxim and New M-Tech from selling White-Westinghouse branded items to major appliance chains, such as Best Buy Co Inc.
The deal marks a major revival of the White-Westinghouse brand name, which has not been previously used on many of the items being sold to Kmart.

Windmere helped both Salton/Maxim and New M-Tech to negotiate licensing and trademark rights for the White-Westinghouse name last year from White Consolidated, a unit of Electrolux AB's Frigidaire unit.
A Kmart spokeswoman would not disclose the size and length of the supply agreement, other than to say it is "long-term."
Salton/Maxim will supply White-Westinghouse brand small kitchen appliances, personal care products, heaters, fans, and electric air cleaners, humidifiers and other products.

New M-Tech will supply White-Westinghouse consumer electronics products including television sets, video cassette recorders, TV/VCR combination units, audio products, portable compact disc players, telephones and telephone answering machines, and other consumer electronics and accessories.

"Kmart is committed to strengthening our franchise with our customers by exclusively offering trusted, market-leader national brands like White-Westinghouse," said Warren Flick, president and chief operating officer of U.S. Kmart Stores.
